intended_object: The colon (quotient) ideal (N : S) = {r ∈ R | r·S ⊆ N} of a submodule N of an R-module M by a subset S (classically by a submodule P). Inferred from the docstring and the name.
explanation: The carrier is exactly the set of r with r • S ⊆ N. It contains 0 (0 • S ⊆ {0} ⊆ N) and is closed under addition ((a+b) • S ⊆ a • S + b • S ⊆ N). It absorbs left multiplication because (s*r) • x = s • (r • x) and N is a submodule. The construction uses only a semiring, an additive commutative monoid and a module structure, which is the maximal natural generality. Over a noncommutative ring, Ideal R means a left ideal, and the colon set is indeed a left ideal. Taking the second argument to be any set rather than a submodule only generalizes the definition; the classical (N : P) is the case S = P. Degenerate cases are correct: S = ∅ gives all of R, and N = ⊥ gives the annihilator of S. The docstring's "P" for the argument named S is a harmless naming slip. This is Mathlib's own canonical definition, and I know of no other Mathlib declaration of the same object.
